why: Integrity means information is accurate and complete, not altered without authorization.

why: A Trojan horse is malware disguised as a legitimate, useful program.
trap: c) describes an attacker (a person), not a program.

why: Ransomware locks or encrypts your files/PC and demands a ransom to unlock them. Only b) describes blocking access + demanding money.

why: Dropping the risky feature entirely removes the risk source, which is risk avoidance. Company A simply doesn't ship the plugin.
trap: c) mitigation is tempting, but mitigation keeps the feature and reduces the risk; here the feature is removed.
cue: Feature removed = avoid; feature fixed = mitigate.

why: CSIRT = Computer Security Incident Response Team: an in-house group that receives security incident reports, investigates and responds.
trap: d) is tempting as another 'global internet body', but that's ICANN; c) is IETF.
cue: CSIRT = 'IR' = Incident Response team.

why: '1'='1' is always true, so the WHERE matches every row and all records are selected. Then '; DROP TABLE accounts' runs a second statement that deletes the whole table.

why: A use case diagram shows actors and the functions (use cases) they perform, plus how those use cases relate (include/extend).
trap: c) interaction overview sounds like 'overview of interactions', but it shows control flow between interactions, not actors.

why: Adapter is a structural pattern that wraps a class to convert its interface into one the client expects, so incompatible classes can work together.

why: Encapsulation bundles data and the methods using it into one object and hides the internal implementation (information hiding).

why: Adaptive maintenance modifies software to keep working when its environment (OS, DBMS, hardware) changes.
trap: d) preventive sounds proactive, but it fixes latent faults before they occur, not environment changes.
cue: Environment changed? Adapt to it.

why: Agile suits small cross-functional teams delivering in short iterations with frequent user feedback on an evolving product.
trap: b) prototyping also uses feedback, but it's for clarifying requirements early, not continuous evolution of all modules.

why: CMMI levels: 1 Initial, 2 Managed, 3 Defined, 4 Quantitatively Managed, 5 Optimizing. Level 5, Optimizing, is the highest.

why: Scope management defines objectives, deliverables, requirements and boundaries, and controls changes to them.
trap: c) Risk is tempting due to 'maximize positive/minimize negative impact', but the impact is from changes to deliverables = scope.

why: Development = 500 FP ÷ 10 = 50 person-months. Add 10 for installation/education = 60. PM adds 10%: 60 × 1.1 = 66.

why: Trend analysis looks at resource usage over time (chronologically) and extrapolates future usage.

why: Availability = system usable when needed. Managing an SLA that defines allowed downtime directly checks availability.

why: BPR radically redesigns and restructures business processes to achieve dramatic gains in productivity, cost, service and quality.

trap: b) the branch staff are senders and change daily; their key would let only them decrypt.

trap: a) uses S[i] + T[i]; a sum, not the difference between the two vectors.

why: Height here counts nodes on the longest path. A perfect tree of height h has 2^h − 1 nodes, so size + 1 = 2^h. Size = left size + right size + 1 (the root).
